content.title: About
content.content: Potato sticks are thin, crunchy slices of potato that are deep‑fried and lightly salted. They have a neutral flavor, making them a versatile snack or ingredient for various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato sticks originated in the United States in the early 1920s as an alternative to potato chips.
Their shape and texture make them a popular base for dips and sauces.
In Russia they are often called “solomka” or “potato solomka.”
To achieve a crisp crust, potatoes are blanched before a quick high‑temperature fry.
Many flavored versions exist, but the plain variety remains the most popular.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives the rapid frying, providing antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in simple sugars
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, plain sticks have low levels of simple sugars.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Starch‑based carbohydrates are rapidly digested, delivering fast energy.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Skin fragments and minor fiber particles aid digestive health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The amount of salt can raise blood pressure; low‑sodium versions are recommended for regular consumption.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Fried sticks contain a notable amount of calories and fat, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oils are used, trans fats may form, which are detrimental to heart health.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to additives used during frying.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Potato sticks can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with dips (ketchup, cheese, yogurt), or added to salads and tartare dishes. Their convenient shape makes them easy to portion.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight bag or container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent oil oxidation.
